facility: Crissey Lock Pumping Station, Canal du Centre, France
source: Arcadis for Voies navigables de France, VNF Crissey Lock Pumping Station Pump Assessment Report, 2020 (Interreg Green WIN public deliverable)
question: VNF plans to replace the out-of-service pumps at Crissey lock pumping station with one new Xylem CT3400/736 submersible pump (nominal 600 l/s) lifting from the River Saône, whose level varies by about six metres. Is this pump a good match for the system and the range of river levels? Would variable speed drives save energy here, given how the pump will be used? What annual energy and saving should we expect compared with the old pump? The proposed discharge arrangement has a DN700 vertical riser with the automated gate valve directly upstream of a DN600 flowmeter, and VNF limits station pipework velocity to 2.2 m/s (CTCG Paper 73): is the pipework right? List the measures you recommend, quantified with the simulator where possible.

alternatives.cost_basis: ASSUMPTION: throttling uses existing automated gate valve (p.7) - no capex, only control logic change. Reason: valve already required.
alternatives.option: A1 - Fixed-speed DOL + gate-valve throttling to cap high-river flow to ~600 l/s
alternatives.result: ALT-THROT-LOW with minor_k 18.0 still passes 744.1 l/s at 94.2 kW electric, 1.93 m/s (run output) vs target 600 l/s (p.5+p.7). Throttling wastes head, holds pump at 122% rated flow warning, efficiency stays low, valve disturbance ruins DN600 meter accuracy. Proves throttling is poor limiter.

alternatives.cost_basis: ASSUMPTION: 110 kW-class LV drive + filters ~EUR 25-40k installed. Reason: no price in pages; typical catalogue for 95.4-96.2 kW input (p.12) size.
alternatives.option: A2 - VSD speed-capped to ~600 l/s at high river (limiter, not energy saver)
alternatives.result: ALT-VSD-080 at speed 0.80: 584.3 l/s, 6.21 m TDH, 55.7 kW electric, 1.52 m/s DN700 (run output) vs fixed-speed Table 1 Minimum 803 l/s, 96.2 kW, 67.3%, 33.3 kWh/1000m3 (p.12). Caps velocity <2.2 m/s (brief limit) and restores meter accuracy, but per-volume energy similar and high-river hours <15% (85% in 172.1-173.1 mNGF p.9), so annual kWh saving <1-2 MWh/yr. Not justified on energy alone.

alternatives.cost_basis: ASSUMPTION: larger 12-pole pump + civils adaptation > CT3400 cost. Reason: 1240 mm vs 830 mm frame (p.11), larger footprint; no price in pages.
alternatives.result: Table 1 Design 604 l/s, 92.7 kW, 78.8%, 42.6 kWh/1000m3 and Minimum 821 l/s, 95.8 kW, 70.5%, 32.4 kWh/1000m3 (p.12) vs CT3400 Design 610 l/s, 95.4 kW, 77.5%, 43.5 (p.12). Still runout ~821 l/s (p.12), same velocity fail, plus power factor 0.52-0.6 vs 0.8-0.82 for CT3400 (p.12) increases cable/transformer burden. Marginal +1.3% eff gain outweighed by electrical penalty.

alternatives.cost_basis: ASSUMPTION: retain as-drawn DN700/DN600 with zero straight length as per brief worst case. Reason: Fig.2 illegible, brief states valve directly upstream of meter (see RFI).
alternatives.option: B0 - Keep proposed DN700 riser + DN600 meter + valve immediately upstream (do nothing)
alternatives.result: Velocity tool: 600 l/s in DN600 = 2.122 m/s (tool output) marginally <2.2 m/s limit, but 803 l/s (p.12) in DN600 = 2.84 m/s (tool output) >2.2 m/s FAIL; 880 l/s old pump (p.14) = 3.112 m/s FAIL. CAL-BASE-MIN sim 887.8 l/s gives 2.31 m/s in DN700 (run output) confirming runout exceeds limit in small meter. Zero straight length violates 5D/3D practice (ASSUMPTION standard, see RFI).

alternatives.cost_basis: ASSUMPTION: short spool + valve move + DN700 electromagnetic meter upsizing during 2020 resize (p.5). Reason: station already under resize; pipework mod order-of-magnitude small vs pump.
alternatives.option: B1 RECOMMENDED - Upsize meter to DN700 and relocate automated gate valve downstream of meter with 5D upstream / 3D downstream straights
alternatives.result: Velocity tool: 600 l/s in DN700 = 1.559 m/s (tool output) <2.2 m/s PASS with margin; 803 l/s (p.12) in DN700 = 2.087 m/s (tool output) <2.2 m/s PASS; CAL-BASE-DES 609.5 l/s gives 1.58 m/s DN700 (run output). Restores meter accuracy, keeps both design 610 l/s (p.12) and runout ~800 l/s (p.11) compliant without throttling.

alternatives.cost_basis: ASSUMPTION: software level + flow interlock in control desk/API (p.7) - no hardware. Reason: automation already required (p.5+p.7).
alternatives.option: B2 - If DN600 retained: enforce flow cap ~600-620 l/s via level-control trip + high-flow alarm from smart monitoring (p.5)
alternatives.result: ALT-VSD-080 proves 584.3 l/s at 55.7 kW holds 1.52 m/s (run output) compliant; CAL-BASE-MAX 542.0 l/s at BWL 171.45 mNGF (p.8) at 87.7 kW, 1.41 m/s (run output) shows low-flow end already compliant. Cap would keep DN600 at ~2.122 m/s at 600 l/s (tool output) but sacrifices free extra flow at high river and still leaves meter disturbed by upstream valve. Inferior to B1.

findings.evidence: Nominal 0.6 m3/s (p.5, p.7) vs Table 1 CT3400/736 Design 610 l/s, 95.4 kW, 77.5%, 43.5 kWh/1000m3 (p.12); Fig.6 intersection ~600 l/s at Design Lift River 172.4 mNGF (p.11); 172.4 lies inside 85% band 172.1-173.1 mNGF (p.9). Illustrative FIX-DES-610 gives 633.7 l/s, 11.05 m TDH, 93.3 kW electric, 1.65 m/s, 40.9 kWh/ML (FIX-DES-610 run output) - order-of-magnitude check only, pipe L=20m C=120 minor_k=3.0 rated_head 11.35m ASSUMPTION (reason: no pipe geometry in pages [5,6,7,8,9,10,11,12,14]). Table 4 (p.14): 880,000 m3/year = 400 basins/year ~408 h/year at 600 l/s (p.14) x 43.5 (p.12) = 38,280 kWh/yr new vs 880 x 52.4 (p.14) = 46,112 kWh/yr old, saving 7,832 kWh/yr quoted directly from Table 4 (p.14). Old baseline Table 3: 880 l/s, 166 kW input, 99 kW hydraulic, 60%, 52.4 kWh/1000m3 (p.14). Document notes running costs typically low given use (p.14).
findings.limiting_value: Design 610 l/s at 77.5% (p.12) vs nominal 600 l/s (p.5); annual Table 4: 38,280 vs 46,112 kWh/yr (p.14)
findings.modification: Approve CT3400/736 for nominal duty - good match at design lift covering 85% operating time. Proceed fixed-speed DOL; do not install VSD for energy saving.

findings.evidence: River varies six metres (p.8); levels Saone high 177.48, low 171.45, pump 170.353, backflow 182.963 mNGF (p.8 Fig.3); System curves Highest BWL 171.45 / Design 172.4 / Lowest TWL 177.48 mNGF (p.11); runout ~800 l/s at minimum lift under fixed speed (p.11) with Table 1 Minimum 803 l/s, 96.2 kW, 67.3%, 33.3 kWh/1000m3, NPSHr 8.22m vs Design NPSHr 4.25m (p.12). Illustrative FIX-MIN-ILLUS gives 921.2 l/s, 6.51 m, 91.9 kW, 2.39 m/s, 151% rated warning (FIX-MIN-ILLUS run output) - overpredicts Table 1 803 l/s (p.12), proving single-point constant-efficiency model invalid far from BEP; do not use sim specific 27.7 kWh/ML, use Table 1 33.3 (p.12). VSD can maintain ~600 l/s regardless of lift (p.12 s.4.2). Illustrative FIX-VSD08-ILLUS at speed 0.80 gives 607.6 l/s, 5.93 m, 55.3 kW, 1.58 m/s (FIX-VSD08-ILLUS run output) with manually set 67.3% (p.12) - limiter illustration only, not affinity prediction. Batch on/off via intermediate + far upstream sensors (p.6) + automation (p.5, p.7) + 85% in 1m band (p.9) + static-dominated = VSD little annual benefit.
findings.limiting_value: 803 l/s runout at 67.3% NPSHr 8.22m (p.12) vs 610 l/s at 77.5% (p.12); ~6m variation (p.8)
findings.modification: If runout must be hard-capped, use VSD as limiter only (~0.80 speed to hold ~600 l/s) with no energy payback; otherwise accept free extra flow. Do not justify VSD on energy.

findings.evidence: Brief-only arrangement: DN700 riser, DN600 meter, automated gate valve (p.7) directly upstream with zero straights - ASSUMPTION (reason: diameters/arrangement/straights not in pages [5,6,7,8,9,10,11,12,14]; brief states valve directly upstream of DN600 meter, Fig.2 illegible). Limit 2.2 m/s + 5D/3D practice - ASSUMPTION per brief/industry norm (reason: not in pages). Velocity tool outputs: 600 l/s in DN600 = 2.122 m/s, 803 l/s (p.12) in DN600 = 2.84 m/s FAIL, 880 l/s (p.14) in DN600 = 3.112 m/s FAIL; 600 l/s in DN700 = 1.559 m/s PASS, 803 l/s in DN700 = 2.087 m/s PASS. FIX-DES-610 1.65 m/s and FIX-VSD08-ILLUS 1.58 m/s in DN700 (run outputs) confirm design compliance in large pipe. Zero straights violates meter accuracy regardless of velocity.
findings.limiting_value: 2.84 m/s in DN600 at 803 l/s (p.12) vs ASSUMPTION 2.2 m/s limit; 0D vs ASSUMPTION 5D/3D
findings.modification: CONDITIONAL on brief: B1 - upsize meter to DN700 and relocate gate valve downstream with 5D/3D straights. Retain DN700 riser. If DN600 retained, enforce flow cap and accept meter disturbance.

findings.evidence: Available pumps have IE2 motors, no IE3 option for these models (p.12) vs target IE3 or IE4 (p.5); CT3400 8-pole pf 0.8-0.82 vs 12-pole alternative pf ~0.52-0.6 (p.12); NPSH margin stated suitable for both (p.12) but suction geometry/levels insufficient to verify - static differences pump 170.353 vs Saone 171.45/177.48 mNGF (p.8) cited without NPSHa calc; submersible monoblock target (p.5). Source naming inconsistent: CT3531/806 ~1240 710mm (p.11) vs CT3500/806 3-1240 710mm Table 1 (p.12) vs CP3531 text (p.12). Smart monitoring + automation/supervision (p.5) + duty/standby level control precedent (p.6) enables verification.
findings.modification: Flag IE non-compliance; require IE3/IE4-compliant equivalent or derogation (prefer CT3400 on pf). Commission with smart energy monitoring: log flow/power/river level to verify 43.5 vs 52.4 (p.12, p.14). Designer to verify NPSHa vs 4.25/8.22m NPSHr (p.12). Note naming inconsistency in procurement.

findings.evidence: Existing 2x RATEAU ID BV 57 (p.6) duty/standby via intermediate + far upstream sensors (p.6) replaced by one new pump nominal 0.6 m3/s (p.5, p.7). With largest (only) unit out, firm capacity zero per definition.
findings.modification: Advise VNF: accept single point of failure or provide standby/mobile provision + maintenance plan for canal level risk. Not quantified - no standby costs/levels in pages.

issues.issue: No NPSHa calculation despite NPSHr rise 4.25 to 8.22m (p.12). At BWL 171.45 mNGF (p.8) with pump 170.353 mNGF (p.8) static submergence ~1.1m (ASSUMPTION arithmetic: 171.45-170.353) < NPSHr, indicating potential margin failure at highest lift. At TWL 177.48 mNGF (p.8) submergence ~7.1m vs NPSHr 8.22m (p.12) also tight. Study repeats document claim margin suitable without verification - missed unit.
issues.evidence: p.8 Fig.3 levels pump 170.353, Saone low 171.45, high 177.48; p.12 NPSHr 4.25m Design 8.22m Minimum

issues.issue: Entire pipework verdict rests on ASSUMPTIONS with no page basis: DN700 riser, DN600 meter, valve directly upstream zero straights (RFI-01), 2.2 m/s limit, 5D/3D rule - none in pages [5,6,7,8,9,10,11,12,14]. Costs <$100k for B1, $100k-$1M for VSD, EUR 0.15/kWh tariff, EUR25-40k drive are ASSUMPTIONS with no page basis. Payback >20yr and EUR1,175/yr saving conclusions depend on invented tariffs/costs. Velocity tool checks themselves are correct (600 in DN600 2.122, 803 in DN600 2.84 FAIL; 600 in DN700 1.559 PASS, 803 in DN700 2.087 PASS) but pass/fail criterion is unverified.
issues.evidence: search_pages DN700=[]; pages contain no diameters; brief-only limit; velocity outputs 2.122/2.84/1.559/2.087/3.112 confirm arithmetic but not criterion

issues.issue: Source uses CT3531/806 ~1240 710mm (p.11 text) vs CT3500/806 3-1240 710mm in Table1 (p.12 image) and CP3531 vs CT3400 in power-factor paragraph (p.12). Study data register carries both D17 CT3531 and D21 CT3500 without flagging source inconsistency.
issues.evidence: view_page p.11 text CT3531/806; view_page p.12 table CT3500/806 3-1240 710mm

issues.item: Annual energy 38,280 vs 46,112 kWh/yr saving 7,832 kWh/yr
issues.issue: Arithmetic correct (880x43.5=38280, 880x52.4=46112 per p.12+p.14) but annualisation assumes all 880,000 m3/year (p.14) at Design 43.5 (p.12). Ignores low-lift specific 33.3/32.4 (p.12) and higher flow ~800 l/s (p.11) reducing hours. 85% band 172.1-173.1 mNGF (p.9) with Design 172.4 (p.11) makes approximation reasonable but low-lift <15% weighting not done - weak assumption, saving overstated/understated by lift mix.
issues.evidence: p.14 880,000m3/year; p.12 Design 43.5 Minimum 33.3; p.9 85% band; p.11 runout ~800 l/s

issues.issue: Like-for-like comparison assumes same lift, but old test head/river level not given. Study RFI-05 notes caveat yet presents firm saving. Old 880 l/s (p.14) vs new 610 l/s Design (p.12) at different heads cannot be normalised from pages. ALT-OLD-880 sim 819.6 vs 880 l/s (-6.86%) using new heads confirms mismatch.
issues.evidence: p.14 Table3 880 l/s 166kW 52.4 without head; p.12 Table1 duties without numeric static lift

issues.item: Alternatives ALT-THROT-LOW and ALT-VSD-080 not truly verified
issues.issue: Throttling minor_k=18.0 ASSUMPTION arbitrary, still passes 744.1 l/s vs 600 l/s target (p.5+p.7), so fails to demonstrate required throttling and valve authority unknown. VSD speed 0.80 result 584.3 l/s 55.7kW uses manually set efficiency 0.673, not affinity-law prediction, and per-m3 26.5 vs 26.3 shows no benefit yet study claims limiter role without addressing BWL 171.45 mNGF (p.8) left-of-BEP risk where CAL-BASE-MAX already 542 l/s.
issues.evidence: logged runs ALT-THROT-LOW, ALT-VSD-080 rerun; p.7 automated gate valve, no characteristic in pages

issues.issue: Existing 2x RATEAU with duty/standby via intermediate+far upstream sensors (p.6) replaced by single pump (p.5+p.7). With largest (only) unit out, firm capacity zero. Study does not assess single point of failure, standby provision, or canal level risk during maintenance.
issues.evidence: p.6 2 pumps duty standby; p.5+p.7 one new pump nominal 0.6m3/s

findings.evidence: Nominal 0.6 m3/s (p.5, p.7) vs Table 1 CT3400/736 Design 610 l/s, 95.4 kW, 77.5%, 43.5 kWh/1000m3 (p.12); Fig.6 intersection ~600 l/s at Design Lift River 172.4 mNGF (p.11); 172.4 lies inside 85% band 172.1-173.1 mNGF (p.9). Illustrative FIX-DES-610 gives 633.7 l/s, 11.05 m TDH, 93.3 kW electric, 1.65 m/s, 40.9 kWh/ML (FIX-DES-610 run output) - order-of-magnitude check only, pipe L=20m C=120 minor_k=3.0 rated_head 11.35m ASSUMPTION (reason: no pipe geometry in pages [5,6,7,8,9,10,11,12,14]). Table 4 (p.14): 880,000 m3/year = 400 basins/year ~408 h/year at 600 l/s (p.14) x 43.5 (p.12) = 38,280 kWh/yr new vs 880 x 52.4 (p.14) = 46,112 kWh/yr old, saving 7,832 kWh/yr quoted directly from Table 4 (p.14). Old baseline Table 3: 880 l/s, 166 kW input, 99 kW hydraulic, 60%, 52.4 kWh/1000m3 (p.14). Document notes running costs typically low given use (p.14).
findings.limiting_value: Design 610 l/s at 77.5% (p.12) vs nominal 600 l/s (p.5); annual Table 4: 38,280 vs 46,112 kWh/yr (p.14)
findings.modification: Approve CT3400/736 for nominal duty - good match at design lift covering 85% operating time. Proceed fixed-speed DOL; do not install VSD for energy saving.

findings.evidence: River varies six metres (p.8); levels Saone high 177.48, low 171.45, pump 170.353, backflow 182.963 mNGF (p.8 Fig.3); System curves Highest BWL 171.45 / Design 172.4 / Lowest TWL 177.48 mNGF (p.11); runout ~800 l/s at minimum lift under fixed speed (p.11) with Table 1 Minimum 803 l/s, 96.2 kW, 67.3%, 33.3 kWh/1000m3, NPSHr 8.22m vs Design NPSHr 4.25m (p.12). Illustrative FIX-MIN-ILLUS gives 921.2 l/s, 6.51 m, 91.9 kW, 2.39 m/s, 151% rated warning (FIX-MIN-ILLUS run output) - overpredicts Table 1 803 l/s (p.12), proving single-point constant-efficiency model invalid far from BEP; do not use sim specific 27.7 kWh/ML, use Table 1 33.3 (p.12). VSD can maintain ~600 l/s regardless of lift (p.12 s.4.2). Illustrative FIX-VSD08-ILLUS at speed 0.80 gives 607.6 l/s, 5.93 m, 55.3 kW, 1.58 m/s (FIX-VSD08-ILLUS run output) with manually set 67.3% (p.12) - limiter illustration only, not affinity prediction. Batch on/off via intermediate + far upstream sensors (p.6) + automation (p.5, p.7) + 85% in 1m band (p.9) + static-dominated = VSD little annual benefit.
findings.limiting_value: 803 l/s runout at 67.3% NPSHr 8.22m (p.12) vs 610 l/s at 77.5% (p.12); ~6m variation (p.8)
findings.modification: If runout must be hard-capped, use VSD as limiter only (~0.80 speed to hold ~600 l/s) with no energy payback; otherwise accept free extra flow. Do not justify VSD on energy.

findings.evidence: Brief-only arrangement: DN700 riser, DN600 meter, automated gate valve (p.7) directly upstream with zero straights - ASSUMPTION (reason: diameters/arrangement/straights not in pages [5,6,7,8,9,10,11,12,14]; brief states valve directly upstream of DN600 meter, Fig.2 illegible). Limit 2.2 m/s + 5D/3D practice - ASSUMPTION per brief/industry norm (reason: not in pages). Velocity tool outputs: 600 l/s in DN600 = 2.122 m/s, 803 l/s (p.12) in DN600 = 2.84 m/s FAIL, 880 l/s (p.14) in DN600 = 3.112 m/s FAIL; 600 l/s in DN700 = 1.559 m/s PASS, 803 l/s in DN700 = 2.087 m/s PASS. FIX-DES-610 1.65 m/s and FIX-VSD08-ILLUS 1.58 m/s in DN700 (run outputs) confirm design compliance in large pipe. Zero straights violates meter accuracy regardless of velocity.
findings.limiting_value: 2.84 m/s in DN600 at 803 l/s (p.12) vs ASSUMPTION 2.2 m/s limit; 0D vs ASSUMPTION 5D/3D
findings.modification: CONDITIONAL on brief: B1 - upsize meter to DN700 and relocate gate valve downstream with 5D/3D straights. Retain DN700 riser. If DN600 retained, enforce flow cap and accept meter disturbance.

findings.evidence: Available pumps have IE2 motors, no IE3 option for these models (p.12) vs target IE3 or IE4 (p.5); CT3400 8-pole pf 0.8-0.82 vs 12-pole alternative pf ~0.52-0.6 (p.12); NPSH margin stated suitable for both (p.12) but suction geometry/levels insufficient to verify - static differences pump 170.353 vs Saone 171.45/177.48 mNGF (p.8) cited without NPSHa calc; submersible monoblock target (p.5). Source naming inconsistent: CT3531/806 ~1240 710mm (p.11) vs CT3500/806 3-1240 710mm Table 1 (p.12) vs CP3531 text (p.12). Smart monitoring + automation/supervision (p.5) + duty/standby level control precedent (p.6) enables verification.
findings.modification: Flag IE non-compliance; require IE3/IE4-compliant equivalent or derogation (prefer CT3400 on pf). Commission with smart energy monitoring: log flow/power/river level to verify 43.5 vs 52.4 (p.12, p.14). Designer to verify NPSHa vs 4.25/8.22m NPSHr (p.12). Note naming inconsistency in procurement.

findings.evidence: Existing 2x RATEAU ID BV 57 (p.6) duty/standby via intermediate + far upstream sensors (p.6) replaced by one new pump nominal 0.6 m3/s (p.5, p.7). With largest (only) unit out, firm capacity zero per definition.
findings.modification: Advise VNF: accept single point of failure or provide standby/mobile provision + maintenance plan for canal level risk. Not quantified - no standby costs/levels in pages.

responses.explanation: Accepted: prior CAL-BASE-DES presented as calibration with -0.08% residual using ASSUMPTION L=120m C=120 minor_k=3.0 motor_eff=0.95. Replaced with FIX-DES-610 (633.7 l/s, 93.3 kW) explicitly labelled illustrative order-check only, pipe data flagged ASSUMPTION (no geometry in pages). No longer claim independent verification; adopt Arcadis curves/Table 1 (p.11, p.12) as basis. Canal reservoir 182.963 mNGF (p.8) retained only to allow EPANET run, not as recomputed head.

Accepted: constant-efficiency single-point model invalid off-BEP. FIX-MIN-ILLUS (921.2 l/s, 151% warning) overpredicts Table 1 Minimum 803 l/s (p.12) by ~15%; sim specific 27.7 vs Table 1 33.3 kWh/1000m3 (p.12) ~17% low rejected. Use Table 1 803 l/s 67.3% 33.3 (p.12) and velocity-tool 2.087 m/s in DN700 for compliance, not sim 2.39 m/s.
responses.issue: Low-lift runout CAL-BASE-MIN vs Table1 Minimum

responses.explanation: Partially accepted: NPSHa not calculated in prior work despite NPSHr 4.25 to 8.22m (p.12) and levels pump 170.353, Saone 171.45/177.48 mNGF (p.8). QA arithmetic (1.1m/7.1m submergence) rejected as NPSHa failure proof - suction arrangement, losses, submersible behaviour unknown; target is submersible monoblock (p.5). Document states margin suitable (p.12) but pages provide no verification data, so flagged as designer check, not proven failure.

Accepted: DN700/DN600/valve-zero-straights, 2.2 m/s, 5D/3D, costs <$100k/$100k-$1M, EUR0.15/kWh all ASSUMPTIONS (brief-only, not in pages). Velocity arithmetic confirmed correct (2.122/2.84/3.112/1.559/2.087) but pass/fail reframed CONDITIONAL on brief limit. Payback >20yr and EUR1,175/yr rejected as firm; annual saving now quoted directly from Table 4 7,832 kWh (p.14) without tariff payback.
Accepted minor: source inconsistent CT3531/806 (p.11) vs CT3500/806 3-1240 (p.12 table) vs CP3531 (p.12 text). Flagged in findings and procurement note; CT3400/736 retained as VNF proposed (p.12).

Accepted weakness: annualisation at Design 43.5 (p.12) for all 880,000 m3 (p.14) ignores Minimum 33.3/32.4 (p.12) and ~800 l/s (p.11) fewer hours. Corrected to quote Table 4 directly (38,280 vs 46,112 saving 7,832 p.14) as document estimate, noting 85% band 172.1-173.1 (p.9) containing Design 172.4 (p.11) makes it reasonable but low-lift <15% weighting not in pages so no refined mix claimed.

responses.explanation: Accepted caveat: old test head/river level not given (p.14 Table 3 880 l/s 166kW 52.4 without head) vs new duties without numeric static lift (p.12), so 52.4 vs 43.5 (p.12, p.14) not normalised. Presented as indicative per-document comparison (Table 4 p.14), not firm like-for-like; prior ALT-OLD-880 sim rejected.
